rationale: C offers the strongest overall balance: clear Simple-first hierarchy, legible required service copy, well-separated contact information, cohesive mountain imagery, and a consistent, production-plausible treatment across all shown views. E is similarly polished but makes some secondary branding and contact details too small. D improves information organization over A, while both give the two brands more equal visual weight than the stated hierarchy suggests; A also uses low-contrast green web copy. B is distinctive and strongly emphasizes Simple, but secondary branding and service copy are undersized, and the visible wording appears less aligned with the required property-management copy.
uncertainty_notes: The supplied images are low resolution, preventing reliable assessment of small-copy legibility, exact wording, and fine production details. Only three views are shown, and the incomplete brief leaves vehicle-side requirements and the intended prominence of Ski On Ski Off somewhat uncertain.
